desk.headline: HEPS up 9.3% to 334.1c on revenue up 2% to R22.5bn; EBITDA margin above target but revenue growth short of it; MTN takeover talks under way
results: Headline earnings per share rose 9.3% to 334.1c and profit rose 10.8% to R1.78bn, as costs were cut and revenue edged up 2% to R22.5bn.
EBITDA grew 5.8% to R6.4bn, lifting the margin 1.1 points to 28.3%; free cash flow jumped 37.8% to R998m.
Mobile service revenue grew 4% to R11.5bn, slowing from 6.4% in the first quarter; mobile data rose 8.7% while voice fell 13.1%. Subscribers rose 7.2% to 26.3m.
Openserve fibre revenue rose 4.2% to R6.6bn, with homes connected up 15.1% to about 871,000; BCX revenue fell 8.2% to R5.4bn and its EBITDA 22.7%.
Capex fell 22.5% to R2.2bn. No interim dividend, as Telkom pays one dividend a year.

guidance.summary: Telkom keeps its medium-term targets set in June 2025 but says outside conditions (energy and fuel prices, inflation, geopolitics) have changed a lot. Revenue growth of 2% is below its mid-single-digit target, the EBITDA margin is above its 25-27% range, and capex should rise in the second half to land in the full-year range.

points: CEO Serame Taukobong said progress is "uneven": voice revenue is falling, mobile growth has slowed and BCX is still being rebuilt.
Telkom blamed civil unrest for disrupting prepaid recharges through informal sellers and is adding national retail chains as outlets.
The voice decline is partly deliberate, with free calls bundled into data packages to push customers to data.
Spending is shifting to getting more from the existing network, such as connecting homes Openserve's fibre already passes.
CFO Nonkululeko Dlamini said the MTN takeover talks are at an early stage and the board is handling them; terms are not settled.
call.source: Results coverage: TechCentral, EWN, BusinessTech and TimesLIVE/Business Day (17 Nov 2026)

watch: Progress of MTN's approach to buy all of Telkom (cash, with an MTN-share option); there is no certainty of a deal.
Whether mobile service revenue growth keeps slowing and prepaid ARPU keeps slipping.
BCX turnaround and the expected rise in second-half capex.
